From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 16:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — security questions

Hi Sam — great questions and thanks for sending the DPA request. Quick answers up front:

- SOC 2: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II (in-scope: Security, Availability). We can share the attestation under an NDA — see attached Redwood_SOC2_Summary_20270422.pdf for a high-level summary.
- DPA & SCCs: Redwood is the processor; Acme Health is the controller. For EU data transfers we typically execute the SCC Clause set appropriate for controller-to-processor relationships (Module 2 / Controller-to-Processor). I'll attach our SCC matrix and a redlined DPA for your review.
- HIPAA: We do not currently operate as a HIPAA Business Associate by default. We can discuss specific controls and potential BAAs with the legal team if Acme needs HIPAA-covered processing.

Next steps:
1) Rishi and I will review the DPA you sent and propose minor edits to align with our standard language.
2) Neha will confirm whether any additional supplementary controls are advisable for healthcare workloads.
3) We'll share a proposed SCC module selection and redlined DPA by Thu 22 Apr.

Are there specific EU entities or hosting locations we should consider when drafting the SCCs?

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_SCC_Matrix_20270421.pdf, Redwood_SOC2_Summary_20270422.pdf

Marissa / Neha — forwarding Acme's DPA request. I'll take the DPA redline and propose standard language. Key items to watch:
- Data flow: Acme will be sending PHI-like healthcare data to Redwood for inference. Need to confirm whether customer data is stored and retention windows.
- Subprocessors: Acme asked about subprocessors and whether SCC Module 3 is applicable for any downstream subprocessor transfers. We should present our current subprocessors list and subprocessors policy.

I'll draft the redlines and share by EOD.

-Rishi
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from demo — security questions

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear ask and the DPA doc. A few clarifications from security/compliance:

1) SOC 2: Confirmed — Type II, Security & Availability. We provide the full report under NDA; I'll include the steps to request it.
2) Controller/Processor role: Redwood will act as a Processor. For transfers, the typical choice is Module 2 (Controller to Processor). That covers controller -> processor transfers and is the correct baseline for Acme as the controller.
3) Subprocessors and Module 3: Module 3 (Processor to Processor) only applies when Redwood transfers data to another processor. We'll include our subprocessors manifest and contract terms. If the customer requires Processor -> Processor SCC language for subprocessors, we can add the relevant clauses or provide subprocessors addendum.
4) HIPAA: We are not currently a HIPAA-covered BAA provider. If Acme expects PHI handling under HIPAA, we need confirmation of the intended data types and volumes so we can evaluate BAAs and potential controls gaps.

I attached a short SCC selection note and our SOC 2 summary for quick reference. Proposed deliverables: redlined DPA (by Rishi), subprocessors list, SOC2 NDA request instructions, and SCC module recommendation (Module 2). Will that timeline work?

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Security & Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_SCC_Matrix_20270421.pdf, Redwood_SOC2_Summary_20270422.pdf

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 16:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA & SCC selection - draft redlines

Sam / Laura — attaching our proposed redline to your DPA (see attached Acme_DPA_Response_20270422.pdf). High-level notes:
- Role: Redwood confirms processor role; we'll add explicit controller/processor language per your template.
- SCCs: We recommend Module 2 (Controller -> Processor) for the primary agreement. If Acme requires processor->processor clauses for any subprocessors, we can add Module 3 language for those specific transfers.
- Subprocessors: Included a current manifest and a commitment to notify 30 days before new subprocessors.
- Retention: Proposed default retention windows and a data deletion workflow; please flag if Acme's legal needs stronger retention terms.

Next: If the redline looks OK, we can circulate to our legal for final sign-off and then route for DocuSign. Otherwise, call to walk through specifics is fine — happy to schedule.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Acme_DPA_Response_20270422.pdf, Redwood_Subprocessors_Manifest_20270422.pdf

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA & SCC selection / controller-processor alignment - Acme Health

Thanks team — appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear recommendations. A few quick decisions from Acme legal: 
- We accept Redwood's processor designation.
- Acme will require Module 2 (Controller->Processor) SCCs for EU personal data transfers.
- For subprocessors that involve cross-border flows, we want the specific P2P (Module 3) clauses appended for those subprocessors only — please include a subprocessors appendix identifying which subprocessors, if any, will trigger P2P clauses.
- Regarding SOC 2, we'll request the full report under NDA (please provide the NDA link and instructions).

Next steps:
1) Rishi — finalize the redline and share DocuSign link.
2) Neha — please send the subprocessors manifest and confirm notification cadence.
3) Marissa — I'll loop in procurement once we have DocuSign.

If you can hit those items by EOD Thu 29 Apr we'll aim to get internal approvals that week.

Best,
Sam
